title: The generic fibre lies in the interiors of the strata
statement: Let $S$ be an integral Noetherian affine scheme [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], $g:Z\to S$ a finite morphism, and $T$ a finite stratification of $Z$ into locally closed constructible strata [def-constructible-stratification]. Write $W=\bigcup_i\operatorname{int}_Z(T_i)$. Every point $x$ with $g(x)=\eta_S$, where $\eta_S$ is the generic point of $S$, belongs to $W$.

source.place: ## Proof, first three paragraphs (closedness, reduction, generic lisse source)

proof.text: The finite source is Noetherian, by finite type over a Noetherian scheme. In particular it has finitely many irreducible components.
Choose an irreducible component C containing x and its generic point c. Continuity makes g(c) specialize to eta_S. The generic point eta_S specializes to g(c), so T0 separation gives g(c)=eta_S.
The finite map has finite fibres and is locally of finite type, so its fibres are discrete. Both c and x lie in the generic fibre and c specializes to x; discreteness gives c=x.

Remove the other finitely many irreducible components to obtain a nonempty open O contained in C; the generic point x of C lies in O. Let T_i contain x. The closed set closure(T_i) contains C. Since T_i is locally closed, coborder(T_i) is open and T_i=coborder(T_i) intersect closure(T_i). Thus O intersect coborder(T_i) is an open neighbourhood of x contained in T_i. Hence x belongs to its interior and to W.

theorem generic_fiber_subset_stratum_interiors
    (S : Scheme.{u}) [IsIntegral S] [IsNoetherian S] [IsAffine S]
    {Z : Scheme.{u}} (g : Z ⟶ S) [IsFinite g] (T : Stratification Z) :
    ∀ x : Z, g x = genericPoint S → x ∈ (T.interiorUnion : Set Z)
